messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: suggestion regarding error messages
parts:
Hi, often when I run Stan I get this error message:

—

Error in rstan::sflist2stanfit(out) :
The following elements of ‘sflist' do not contain samples: 1, 2, 3, 4.

—

And it’s hard for me to figure out what this means. Often this is a signal that I’ve forgot to specify something in the data, or that some of the data objects in R are the wrong size or the wrong shape or have missingness. In this case it turned out there was a problem in the model where I’d screwed up on an index for a matrix and was looking for an element that wasn’t there (it was a 50x13 matrix and I was looking for something with first index 51). So if it’s possible to make this error message more specific it could be helpful, as I see it a lot and it can be hard to find. (This one took me 1/2 hour to debug.)

Thx
A

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] suggestion regarding error messages
parts:
I agree that shouldn't be the only output. There's a bug
somewhere with an error either not getting caught or getting
caught and inadvertently ignored. This kind of thing we want
to really concentrate on fixing to make user debugging as
easy as possible.

When you say looking for an index that's not there, you mean
you had Stan code like x[n] where n was beyond the range of
the array? And if so, in transformed data or later? Do you recall
other situations where you've gotten this message?

Stan should be throwing an exception here with the specifics.
If it's not, there should be an issue filed with stan to fix it,
otherwise an issue with rstan to fix on that side.

- Bob

parts:
> On May 8, 2015, at 5:39 PM, Andrew Gelman <Gel...@stat.columbia.edu> wrote:
>
>
>> On May 8, 2015, at 10:43 AM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
>>
>> When you say looking for an index that's not there, you mean
>> you had Stan code like x[n] where n was beyond the range of
>> the array? And if so, in transformed data or later? Do you recall
>> other situations where you’ve gotten this message?
>
> Yes, it was x[n] where n was beyond the range. I think it was in the model block but I’m not sure. Usually when I get this message it’s because I’m not sending the correct size or shape of data from R when calling Stan.

There are two places things can go wrong. If it's
in transformed data, you'll get an error when trying to
instantiate the Stan program with data.

If it's after that (transformed parameters, model, generated
quantities), then it'll show up whenever that code gets executed,
which is usually the first iteration.

- Bob
